where: Section 3, the ratio form of Chvorinov's rule
problem: The exponent is written flat: t₂/t₁ = [(V/A)₂/(V/A)₁]n. A student can read the trailing 'n' as multiplication by n instead of a power, and this form is the one used all through the worked example and Q3 and Q7.
fix: Write t₂/t₁ = [(V/A)₂/(V/A)₁]<sup>n</sup> so the power is clear, matching the main formula t = B (V/A)<sup>n</sup>.

problem: The text uses a caret, '(length ratio)^n'. Caret notation is not an inline superscript and looks like a typo on a phone screen.

A is defined only as 'the heat-losing surface area'. Students often take the whole outer surface even for a riser or a casting joined to a gating system, where the contacting face does not lose heat to the mould.
fix: Say: A is the surface area through which heat actually leaves the metal, that is the area in contact with the mould; a face joined to the riser or gate does not count.
